title: Independent-encryptor audit, part 2: 3,192 K4-shaped messages from textbook encryptors (no shared code) fed to the test functions of attacks 54, 56, 57, 59, 60, 61, 62, 65, 68, 69, 70, 73, 74, 78, 79, 81, 84, 86, 88, 89, 90, plus 918 messages mapping two stacked keys
k4_result: Not applicable: no K4 search, nothing decrypted. The audit found no convention mistake in any of the 21 attacks (clue positions, alphabet direction, index letter, Beaufort sign, gap direction, wheel sizes and grid offsets agree with the textbook encryptors, which themselves reproduce K1-K3, the carved tableau and Byrne's Chaocipher example). It found scope smaller than claimed in attacks 57/80, 59, 60C, 61, 69B, 88, 90 and in the stacked-key rule inside 68, 70, 78, 81, 88; one of these (attack 90) is a real bug.
controls: Shuffled K4s do not apply (no K4 score to compare). Controls of the audit itself: (1) 96 messages with the clue words one letter late, through 16 attack tests (59, 68 x2, 70, 81, 90, 54, 56, 61, 62, 65, 69, 73, 84, 86, 89): 0 found, as it must be; (2) decoy alphabets handed over with each true one (40; 8-10 for 73, 81, 89): a decoy alphabet was listed for 12 of 1,776 messages, 2 of them identity messages (sliding move 0, multiplier 1) that fit every alphabet; (3) every planted alphabet is in the list the attack really runs on (0 missing of 666,993 dictionary and 140,752 non-keyword alphabets); (4) 11/11 checks of the new textbook encryptors.
planted: 2711/3192 found; 261 more had too few checks to be judged; 220 missed with enough checks. By attack (found/planted, limit, missed): 54 192/192; 56 95/96 (1 limit); 57 168/240 (72 missed); 59 62/120 (38, 20); 60A 72/72; 60B 37/72 (35 limit); 60C 48/72 (24 missed); 61 107/144 (23, 14); 62 24/48 (24 limit); 65 85/120 (35 limit); 68 334/336 (2 missed); 69A 18/24 (6 limit); 69B 48/72 (24 missed); 70 192/192; 73 96/96; 74 edges 60/96 (36 limit); 78 test 68 69/72 (3 missed); 78 test 70 120/120; 79 96/96; 81 274/288 (4, 10); 84 68/72 (4 limit); 86 46/48 (2 limit); 88 128/168 (2, 38); 89 96/96; 90 176/240 (51, 13). Stacked-key maps (every pair p<q<=13, one message per pair and setting): 380 of 680 judgeable messages missed (68: 123 of 242 over six gaps; 70: 100 of 205 over N=27..31; 81: 77 of 114; 88: 80 of 119).
scope_limits: Audits the test functions only, not the full enumeration loops and not the English-scoring stages. Attacks 54 and 79 (formula part) were handed the true ingredients plus 8 decoy ingredients through work(); 56 the true tableau plus 4 decoys; 61 the job that holds the planted scramble; 86 one keyword length per message with a 2-million-step budget; 57 only the convention (are the planted key letters among the 28 readings), 80 only through 57's views. Not audited: 55, 58, 67, 75-77, 82, 83, 85; 74 only at the edges idea 91 did not draw; 78 only its tests 68 (3 cells) and 70 (5 cells); 89 only its battery part (not the key-text score or the join). 24 messages per model, alphabets from 46 audit words, decoys instead of the full alphabet lists. 'Too few checks' uses each attack's own threshold. A miss means K4 was not tested at that setting; it says nothing about K4.

negative.family: Method audit (shared conventions in planted tests), part 2
negative.hypothesis: The exact clue tests of attacks 54-62, 65, 68-70, 73, 74, 78, 79, 81, 84, 86, 88-90 share a convention mistake with their own planting code, or cover less than their negatives say, so they pass their planted tests and would still miss the real K4.
negative.scope: Textbook encryptors written from the definitions with no code from the attacks (kryptos/idea91_textbook.py, kryptos/idea105_textbook.py; checked against the carved K1-K3, the tableau and Byrne's Chaocipher example): autokey + repeating key, the round-11 key rules on each clue alone / with the gap off by 1-3 / on wheels of 27-31 cells / with one wrong clue letter / with the key running over word spaces, row-keys-row autokey, key formulas, interrupted key, switching and interleaved systems, Slidefair, scrambled key, drifting key, chain addition, row + column words, rows of 21, changing alphabets and Chaocipher, two layers on two tableaux, keyword-tail solver, keyphrase alphabets, English running key; 3,192 K4-shaped messages (24 per model, 133 models) plus 918 stacked-key messages through each attack's own test function.
negative.outcome: Dead as a convention mistake: none found in 21 attacks; attacks 54, 56, 60A, 60B, 62, 65, 69A, 73, 74, 79, 84, 86, 89 and every rule of 70 but the stacked keys found every judgeable plant (controls: 96 messages with the clue one letter late, 0 found; shuffled K4s do not apply; planted 2711/3192 found, 261 unjudgeable, 220 missed). Scope holes: (1) attack 90 has a bug in _order() (runs split on the clue index, not the position): cipher feed 30-33 back with a word of 2-4 on top is never tested (13/13 missed, about 440 million settings); (2) attack 59 skips any lag with fewer than 12 usable letters: cipher feed 34-60 and plain feed 7-8 are untested (20 missed), plain feed 9 cannot be judged; (3) attack 88: a progressive key is untested once word breaks leave no two clue letters p apart in one run (lengths 6-12 with EAST|NORTH|EAST + BERLIN|CLOCK, 24/24 missed), and two stacked keys are missed at 80 of 119 judgeable pairs; (4) the stacked-key pre-filter of idea 91's hole (a) repeats in 68 (123 of 242 missed), 70 (100 of 205), 78 and 81 (77 of 114); (5) 60C misses a Slidefair message whenever a clue pair uses the same-column rule (24/24; about 35% of real messages); (6) 61 tests the quarter turn one way only (14 of 23 missed the other way); (7) 69B finds a different tableau per row only if the column key is a number or both rows share the cipher strip (24/24 missed otherwise); (8) 57 and 80 read the key letter on M or KRYPTOS only if it was set under the first letter of the plain strip (72/72 missed with the key under plain A on M/M, M/KR, KR/M). Claimed but never judgeable: 65 taps 9-10 back, 69A shifts -5 and -4, 62 widths 10+ (as its docstring says).

follow_ups: Fix the bug in attack 90 and rerun the hole: in kryptos/idea90_rowkey.py _order(), break runs on the position (pr[1] == cur[-1][1] + 1), not on the clue index pr[0]. Then run K4 and the three shuffled thirds on cipher feed 30, 31, 32, 33 letters back with a word of 2, 3 or 4 on top (11 (lag, word) settings x 666,993 alphabets x 5 layouts x Vigenere/Beaufort x feed numbering M/A-Z/KRYPTOS x sign, about 440 million settings, a few minutes). Planted test: kryptos.idea105_audit.Audit.plant_90('cipher', 30, 33) must be found 24/24 (now 11/24).

Close the hole in attack 59 (autokey + repeating key on A-Z/KRYPTOS): delete 'if len(use) < 12: continue' so the check count alone decides, and run cipher feed 34-60 letters back (11 usable clue letters; key lengths 1-5 give 6-10 checks) and plain feed 7 (key 1-4) and 8 (key 1-2) letters back, multiplier 1-25, 10 shuffled controls. Planted test: Audit.plant_59('cipher', 34, 60) and plant_59('plain', 7, 9).

Progressive key when no two clue letters lie p apart in one unbroken run: kryptos.round11.battery (and idea88_slip._tables) take the step only from such a pair. Take it instead from any two clue letters at the same place mod p in different passes (or try all 25 steps). Rerun attack 88 for lengths 6-12 with EAST|NORTH|EAST + BERLIN|CLOCK, 9-12 with EAST|NORTHEAST + BERLIN|CLOCK and 11-12 with BERLINCLOCK unbroken, and attack 81 for lengths 11-12 with a wrong letter inside EASTNORTHEAST. Planted test: Audit.plant_88('progressive', p1=2, p2=1, pmin=6, pmax=12) must be found 24/24 (now 0/24).

Two stacked keys with the exact solve instead of the c1 + c2 pre-filter (idea 91's follow-up 1), extended to the battery's other users: gap off by -3..+3 (attack 68: 20-21 pairs missed per gap), wheels of 27-31 cells (attack 70: the same 20 pairs, and only a necessary test there), one wrong clue letter (attack 81: 24-27 of 38 pairs) and the key running over word spaces (attack 88: 24-29 of 39-40 pairs, even 4,5 and 3,7). Planted test: Audit.stacked_map for '68', '70', '81', '88' must miss nothing.

Smaller convention gaps, each a few lines: (a) attack 60 Slidefair: accept the ACA same-column rule (a pair may also be C1 = P1 + 1, C2 = P2 + 1), since about 35% of real Slidefair messages have such a pair inside the clues; (b) attack 61: add the quarter turn the other way (columns from the left, read upwards); (c) attack 69 part B: join on the key LETTERS found on each row's own cipher strip (26 offsets per row) as well as on key numbers; (d) attacks 57 and 80: also read the key letter as M[s + c] and KRYPTOS[s + c] for the offset c of plain A (key set under A, the ACA way) on M/M, M/KR and KR/M.
